Position: Cabinet Maker
Type: Full-time
Employer: Final Touch Joinery Pty Ltd
Location: Kenthurst NSW 2156
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
Final Touch Joinery Pty Ltd is a reputable North-West Sydney-based cabinetry specialist established in 2006 by Director Nathan Diab. With a strong commitment to quality craftsmanship and exceptional customer service, the company specialises in custom kitchen joinery, wardrobes, vanities, and architectural fit-outs for both residential and commercial clients, including high-end homes, unit developments, pubs, clubs, and insurance repair projects. Using premium materials and advanced CAD software, Final Touch Joinery delivers tailored solutions that bring clients’ visions to life with precision, durability, and elegant finishes. The business prides itself on a collaborative, detail-oriented workplace culture where innovation meets traditional joinery skills in a supportive environment focused on excellence and client satisfaction.
About the Position:
The Cabinet Maker plays a vital role in fabricating, assembling, and installing high-quality custom cabinetry, kitchens, wardrobes, and other joinery solutions for Final Touch Joinery’s diverse residential and commercial projects. Working from detailed drawings and client specifications, this position contributes directly to creating functional, beautiful spaces that meet the highest standards of finish and craftsmanship, helping the company maintain its reputation for premium, personalised results in the joinery industry.
Key Responsibilities:
Examining drawings, work orders, and sample parts to determine specifications.
Selecting and working with materials such as timber, veneers, particle board, laminates, and other engineered wood products.
Marking out, cutting, shaping, and assembling components using hand tools, power tools, and computer numerical control (CNC) machines where applicable.
Fabricating and installing kitchen, bathroom, and other cabinetry, wardrobes, counters, and fittings.
Fitting hinges, locks, catches, drawers, shelves, and other hardware with precision.
Ensuring all work meets quality standards, safety requirements, and client expectations.
Collaborating with the team on commercial and residential fit-outs, including repairs and custom solutions.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum Certificate III in Cabinet Making and Installation, Joinery, or any relevant field or at least 2 years of relevant experience.
Minimum 2 years of experience as a cabinet maker or in a related field.
Strong technical skills in reading technical drawings, precise measurement, woodworking machinery operation, and use of hand/power tools.
Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to quality craftsmanship.
Good interpersonal and communication skills to collaborate effectively with team members and understand client requirements.
Physical fitness and ability to work safely in a workshop and on-site environment.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

•	Strong connection to our corporate culture and understanding of our values and ideals.
•	Accountability, autonomy, responsibility and adaptability are sought after qualities in the right candidate 

Remuneration/Salary

•	Package to include vehicle allowance

result.description:
Australian Fishing Enterprises (AFE) is the largest exporter of Southern Bluefin Tuna in Australia. Our tuna is exported around the world for sale in international marketplaces as a premium sushi/ sashimi product. We specialise in the fishing, ranching and grow out of Southern Bluefin Tuna and control the entire process from catching, feeding, harvesting, processing and delivery.
AFE 5 positions available for this role.

JOB SUMMARY:
The deckhand will carry out duties as directed by the Farm Manager or Vessel Masters.

OPERATIONS:
Periods at sea are varied and weather dependent. Hours of operation are determined by the daily operational needs.
Farm Operations:
Farm vessels can be required to conduct operations year round from land based sites out to the farming site. The season begins in December finishing with the annual harvest period throughout June, July & August.
January – July Operations are 7 days per week; you can work up to 6 days in a week. Up to 12 hours per day.
August to December Operations are 5 days per week Monday to Friday, you will work up to 5 days in a week, 8 hours per day

Offshore Operations:
Tow & Support operations begin in December through to late March. If Quota is exhausted quickly the Offshore Operations will cease before late March.
Hours of operation whilst at Sea are from Sunrise to Sunset plus a navigational watch. There are however periods of downtime.

CONTRACT PERIOD:
Approximate start date: AFE are offering start dates in November, December, January, February, March and April  for up to 9 Months

DUTIES:
The Employee will be required to perform the following duties whilst at sea on the Farm site.
• Ability to stand on unstable surfaces and undertake general duties on a day-to-day basis as advised by the Master
• Forklift operation (license required) onshore only (not essential but desirable)
• Loading and unloading of vessel at sea and on-shore
• Fish feeding, harvesting & processing
• Maintenance as directed by Vessel Engineer
• Repetitive manual labour
• Vessel cleaning and house keeping
• Vessel mooring/berthing
• Net mending
• Rope work (splicing, knotting etc.)
• Farm pontoon maintenance

OFFSHORE DUTIES:
The Employee will be required to perform the following duties whilst at Sea for Offshore Operations.
Navigation Watch:
• Keeping Lookout for other Vessels
• Maintaining Vessel Course as per Master’s instructions
• Vessel Log recording
• Watch Handover to next watch keeper
• Reporting to the Master
• Radio frequency monitoring

A Navigational watch can per performed at any time throughout the day or night, they are generally 1.5-2 hours in duration.
Deck Duties:
• Ability to stand on unstable surfaces and undertake general duties on a day-to-day basis as advised by the Master
• Tender vessel operation
• Launch and retrieval of tender
• Fish Sampling/Chumming
• Maintenance as directed by Vessel Engineer
• Repetitive Manual labour
• Vessel cleaning and house keeping
• Vessel Mooring/Berthing
• Net mending

Hours of operation whilst at Sea are from Sunrise to Sunset plus a navigational watch. There are however downtime periods. For example, if the vessel is steaming to different fishing grounds or is at anchor for the day due to weather the crew can indulge in R&R but will still be required to man a navigational watch in the evening.

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to the role.

INDUCTION & TRAINING:
• All crew are inducted onto the vessel prior to departure
• Safety drills conducted bi-monthly
• Deck machinery training and instruction conducted
• SOP’s to be discussed for operations

REMUNERATION:
FARM OPERATIONS
Renumeration is paid as per the Award Rate, paid on a fortnightly basis. Farm work completed inshore and onshore will be calculated at the applicable hourly Farm rate. Aquaculture Award:(https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000114.html)(https://calculate.fairwork.gov.au/payguides/fairwork/ma000114
OFFSHORE OPERATIONS
An additional contract is put in place alongside original Deckhand Contract to cover the periods Offshore for Tow & Support operations to classify Duties and Remuneration (there is no Award that covers the "At Sea" roles), contract renumeration is calculated from experience and seamanship knowledge.

This is not a FIFO position. Successful applicants will need to based in Port Lincoln for the duration of the contracted period.
result.title: Deckhand

result.description:
Australian Fishing Enterprises (AFE) is the largest exporter of Southern Bluefin Tuna in Australia. Our tuna is exported around the world for sale in international marketplaces as a premium sushi/sashimi product. We specialise in the fishing, ranching and grow out of Southern Bluefin Tuna and control the entire process from catching to feeding, harvesting, processing and delivery. 

JOB SUMMARY:
The deckhand will carry out duties as directed by the Farm Manager or Vessel Masters.

OPERATIONS:
Periods at sea are varied and weather dependent. Hours of operation are determined by the daily operational needs. Farm vessels can be required to conduct operations year round from land based sites out to the farming site. The season begins in December finishing with the annual harvest period throughout June, July & August.
January – July Operations are 7 days per week; you can work up to 6 days in a week. Up to 12 hours per day.
August to December Operations are 5 days per week Monday to Friday, you will work up to 5 days in a week, 8 hours per day.
Offshore Operations:
Tow & Support operations begin in December through to late March. If Quota is exhausted quickly the Offshore Operations will cease before late March.
Hours of operation whilst at Sea are from Sunrise to Sunset plus a navigational watch. There are however periods of downtime.


Approximate start date: December 2026, January - March 2027, AFE will be taking successful candidates throughout 2026/27 for these positions. Employment may be up to 4 years.
For Fulltime positions experience is preferred but not essential, all Candidates will be considered but industry experience is advantageous.
DUTIES:
The Employee will be required to perform the following duties whilst at sea on farm site;
•	Ability to stand on unstable surfaces and undertake general duties on a day-to-day basis as advised by the Master 
•	Forklift operation (license required) onshore only
•	Loading and unloading of vessel at sea and on-shore
•	Fish feeding, harvesting & processing
•	Maintenance as directed by Vessel Engineer
•	Repetitive manual labour 
•	Vessel cleaning and house keeping 
•	Vessel mooring/berthing 
•	Net mending 
•	Rope work (splicing, knotting etc.)
•	Farm pontoon maintenance

OFFSHORE DUTIES:
The Employee will be required to perform the following duties whilst at Sea for Offshore Operations.
Navigation Watch:
• Keeping Lookout for other Vessels
• Maintaining Vessel Course as per Master’s instructions
• Vessel Log recording
• Watch Handover to next watch keeper
• Reporting to the Master
• Radio frequency monitoring
A Navigational watch can per performed at any time throughout the day or night, they are generally 1.5-2 hours in duration.

Deck Duties:
• Ability to stand on unstable surfaces and undertake general duties on a day-to-day basis as advised by the Master
• Tender vessel operation
• Launch and retrieval of tender
• Fish Sampling/Chumming
• Maintenance as directed by Vessel Engineer
• Repetitive Manual labour
• Vessel cleaning and house keeping
• Vessel Mooring/Berthing
• Net mending

Hours of operation whilst at Sea are from Sunrise to Sunset plus a navigational watch. There are however downtime periods. For example, if the vessel is steaming to different fishing grounds or is at anchor for the day due to weather the crew can indulge in R&R but will still be required to man a navigational watch in the evening.

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to the role.

INDUCTION & TRAINING:
•	All crew are inducted onto the vessel prior to departure
•	Safety drills conducted bi-monthly
•	Deck machinery training and instruction conducted 
•	SOP’s to be discussed for operations 

REMUNERATION:
Renumeration is paid as per the Award Rate, paid on a fortnightly basis. Farm work completed inshore and onshore will be calculated at the applicable hourly Farm rate. Aquaculture Award:(https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000114.html)(https://calculate.fairwork.gov.au/payguides/fairwork/ma000114/pdf)
OFFSHORE OPERATIONS
An additional contract is put in place alongside original Deckhand Contract to cover the periods Offshore for Tow & Support operations to classify Duties and Remuneration (there is no Award that covers the "At Sea" roles), contract renumeration is calculated from experience and seamanship knowledge.

This is not a FIFO position. Successful applicants will need to based in Port Lincoln for the duration of the contracted period.
